insights: The table has 10,299 rows and 563 columns: one target column, one subject identifier, and 561 engineered motion-sensor features.

The detailed profile covers only a prefix of columns, but the full schema contains all 561 sensor features; the plan should not truncate to the profiled prefix.

config.preparation: No joins or derived columns are needed. Use the single uploaded table. Retain all 561 numeric sensor features and exclude the target column 'activity' and the group column 'subject'. Use a reproducible group holdout by 'subject' so the same person does not appear in both training and validation/final evaluation. Apply standard preprocessing initially: median imputation, bounded one-hot encoding, and scaling. No augmentations are proposed for the first trial.
config.rationale: The objective is to predict activity for unseen people, so the validation design must keep subjects disjoint. A group holdout by 'subject' directly tests generalization to new persons and avoids leakage from repeated measurements of the same individual. Macro F1 is the appropriate primary metric because it treats all six activity classes equally and is sensitive to confusion between less frequent or visually similar activities such as sitting and standing. All 561 provided sensor features are retained because they are already engineered and the user explicitly asked not to truncate to the profiled prefix. Random Forest, LightGBM, and XGBoost are strong CPU tabular baselines for high-dimensional correlated features, while the regularized linear classifier provides a simple scaled control. Standard preprocessing is used initially as requested; later trials can use confusion-matrix diagnostics, feature subsets, or model-specific parameters if sitting/standing confusion remains high.
